newsitem.title: USA: U.S. lawmakers urge restrictions on Mexican trucks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. lawmakers urge restrictions on Mexican trucks.

text.p: A majority of U.S. House members support continued restrictions on access to U.S. highways for Mexican trucks because of safety concerns, Rep. James Oberstar, D-Minn., said Wednesday.

Oberstar said 226 House members from both parties had signed a letter to President Clinton urging him not to lift current restrictions. They cited a General Accounting Office study which found that unsafe Mexican trucks were crossing the U.S. border without being inspected in Mexico. The GAO is the investigating agency of Congress.

"Very few among the thousands of Mexican trucks crossing into the U.S. daily are inspected," Oberstar said in a statement. "Of those few, 45 pct are ordered out of service. No one wants to face the potential nightmare of Mexican trucks falling apart throughout the United States at 65 miles per hour."
Oberstar is the senior Democrat on the House Transportation Committee.
